Flat posterized portraits — shard-count sweep, 15 to 300 per wall

These flat, bold versions reproduce far better than the real paintings. Recognisable at a handful of shards; crisper as you add more, up to your 300/wall budget. Judge by eye — SSIM is flat (~0.75 / ~0.48) across the entire range and tells you nothing here.

Low end — finding the floor

The Pearl becomes recognisable (scarf + face + jacket) at ~24-30 shards. The Mona is softer because its flat source already has a near-featureless face.

High end — up to your 300/wall budget

More shards keep helping, but gently — the Pearl at 300 has a clear face, eye, scarf and collar; the Mona resolves the figure and arms. The big jump ("blob → recognisable") happens by ~80; everything above that is polish.

Recommendation

shards / wallresultuse it?
~30minimum recognisableproof-of-concept only
~80clearly readable, cleansafe, cheap build
~200-300crispest — Pearl looks genuinely goodbest within your 300 budget

Bottom line: unlike the real paintings (which needed thousands and never fit), these flat portraits are comfortably buildable across the whole range. Use ~80 for a simple piece, or push to ~250-300 for the sharpest result you can still fabricate. The Pearl is the stronger of the two — bold shapes with clear features; the flat Mona's face stays soft because the source itself is.
